requirements.subject: ent:fn-enum2int
requirements.canonical: The `enum2int` predefined function has the signature enum2int(in Enumerated_type inpar) return integer.
requirements.original: enum2int(in Enumerated_type inpar) return integer

requirements.subject: ent:fn-enum2int
requirements.canonical: The `enum2int` function SHALL accept an enumerated value as its `inpar` parameter.
requirements.original: This function accepts an enumerated value and returns the integer value associated to the enumerated value (see also clause 6.2.4).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-enum2int
requirements.canonical: The `enum2int` function SHALL return the integer value associated to the enumerated value passed to `inpar`.
requirements.original: This function accepts an enumerated value and returns the integer value associated to the enumerated value (see also clause 6.2.4).

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: The actual parameter passed to the `inpar` parameter of `enum2int` SHALL always be a typed object.
requirements.original: The actual parameter passed to inpar always shall be a typed object (see clause 6.2.4 and the definition "type context" in clause 3.1).

ambiguity.issue: 'typed object' is not defined in clause 3.1; the sentence refers to the glossary term 'type context', so the intended meaning is an enumerated value whose type is known from its context or a type prefix.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-enum2int
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 apply to the `enum2int` function.
requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-oct2unichar
requirements.canonical: The `oct2unichar` predefined function has the signature oct2unichar(in octetstring invalue, in charstring string_encoding := "UTF-8") return universal charstring.
requirements.original:
oct2unichar(in octetstring invalue, in charstring string_encoding := "UTF-8")
   return universal charstring

requirements.subject: ent:fn-oct2unichar
requirements.canonical: The `oct2unichar` function SHALL convert the octetstring `invalue` to a universal charstring by use of the given `string_encoding`.
requirements.original: This function converts an octetstring `invalue to a universal` `charstring by use of the given` string_encoding.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-oct2unichar
requirements.canonical: The `oct2unichar` function SHALL interpret the octets of `invalue` as mandated by the standardized mapping associated with the given `string_encoding`.
requirements.original: The octets are interpreted as mandated by the standardized mapping associated with the given string_encoding and the resulting characters are appended to the returned value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-oct2unichar
requirements.canonical: The `oct2unichar` function SHALL append the characters resulting from the interpretation of the octets to the returned value.
requirements.original: The octets are interpreted as mandated by the standardized mapping associated with the given string_encoding and the resulting characters are appended to the returned value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-oct2unichar
requirements.canonical: If the optional `string_encoding` parameter of `oct2unichar` is omitted, its value IS the default value "UTF-8".
requirements.original: If the optional string_encoding parameter is omitted, the default value "UTF-8".

ambiguity.issue: The source sentence is grammatically incomplete (verb missing); the meaning is clear from the signature.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: The actual parameter passed to the `string_encoding` parameter of `oct2unichar` SHALL be one of "UTF-8", "UTF-16", "UTF-16LE", "UTF-16BE", "UTF-32", "UTF-32LE" or "UTF-32BE".
requirements.original: The following values (see ISO/IEC 10646 [2]) are allowed as string_encoding actual parameters (for the description of the codepoints see clause 27.5): a) "UTF-8" b) "UTF-16" c) "UTF-16LE" d) "UTF-16BE" e) "UTF-32" f) "UTF-32LE" g) "UTF-32BE"

requirements.subject: ent:fn-oct2unichar
requirements.canonical: The `invalue` parameter of `oct2unichar` SHALL NOT include the optional signature (byte order mark) of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: The invalue parameter shall not include the optional signature (see clause 10 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2], also known as byte order mark).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-oct2unichar
requirements.canonical: When `string_encoding` is "UTF-16" or "UTF-32", the `oct2unichar` function SHALL use big-endian ordering.
requirements.original: In case of "UTF-16" and "UTF-32" big-endian ordering shall be used (as described in clauses 10.4 and 10.7 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2]).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-oct2unichar
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 apply to the `oct2unichar` function.
requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-oct2unichar
requirements.canonical: The universal charstring returned by `oct2unichar` CAN contain non-graphical characters, which cannot be presented between double quotes.
requirements.original: NOTE: The character string returned may contain non-graphical characters, which cannot be presented between the double quotes.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-unichar2oct
requirements.canonical: The `unichar2oct` predefined function has the signature unichar2oct(in universal charstring invalue, in charstring string_encoding := "UTF-8") return octetstring.
requirements.original:
unichar2oct(in universal charstring invalue, in charstring string_encoding := "UTF-8") 
  return octetstring

requirements.subject: ent:fn-unichar2oct
requirements.canonical: The `unichar2oct` function SHALL convert the universal charstring `invalue` to an octetstring.
requirements.original: This function converts a universal `charstring` `invalue to an octetstring.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-unichar2oct
requirements.canonical: The octetstring returned by `unichar2oct` SHALL contain the octets mandated by mapping the characters of `invalue` with the standardized mapping associated with the given `string_encoding`, in the same order as the characters appear in `invalue`.
requirements.original: Each octet of the octetstring` will contain the octets mandated by mapping the characters of invalue using the standardized mapping associated with the given string_encoding in the same order as the characters appear in inpar.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence refers to the parameter 'inpar', which does not exist in the signature of unichar2oct; 'invalue' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-unichar2oct
requirements.canonical: If the optional `string_encoding` parameter of `unichar2oct` is omitted, its value IS the default value "UTF-8".
requirements.original: If the optional string_encoding parameter is omitted, the default value "UTF-8".

ambiguity.issue: The source sentence is grammatically incomplete (verb missing); the meaning is clear from the signature.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: The actual parameter passed to the `string_encoding` parameter of `unichar2oct` SHALL be one of "UTF-8", "UTF-16", "UTF-16LE", "UTF-16BE", "UTF-32", "UTF-32LE" or "UTF-32BE".
requirements.original: The following values (see ISO/IEC 10646 [2]) are allowed as string_encoding actual parameters (for the description of the UCS encoding scheme see clause 27.5): a) "UTF-8" b) "UTF-16" c) "UTF-16LE" d) "UTF-16BE" e) "UTF-32" f) "UTF-32LE" g) "UTF-32BE"

requirements.subject: ent:fn-unichar2oct
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 apply to the `unichar2oct` function.
requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-any2unistr
requirements.canonical: The `any2unistr` predefined function has the signature any2unistr(in template any invalue, in universal charstring format := "") return universal charstring.
requirements.original:
any2unistr(in template any invalue,
          in universal charstring format := "") return universal charstring

requirements.subject: ent:fn-any2unistr
requirements.canonical: The `any2unistr` function SHALL convert the content of a value or template passed to `invalue` to a single universal charstring.
requirements.original: This function converts the content of a value or template to a single universal charstring.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-any2unistr
requirements.canonical: The universal charstring resulting from `any2unistr` IS the same as the string produced by the `log` operation containing the same operand as the one passed to `any2unistr`.
requirements.original: The resulting universal charstring is the same as the string produced by the log operation containing the same operand as the one passed to the any2unistr function.

readings: The result of any2unistr IS always the same as the string produced by the log operation for the same operand.
The result of any2unistr IS the same as the string produced by the log operation for the same operand only when the format parameter is missing or empty.
ambiguity.issue: The unconditional statement conflicts with the format-dependent rules of C.1.33-s007/s008; the second reading (default behaviour) was chosen as consistent with the rest of the clause, but the canonical text keeps the unconditional wording of the source.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-any2unistr
requirements.canonical: The value or template passed to the `invalue` parameter of `any2unistr` MAY be uninitialized, partially initialized or completely initialized.
requirements.original: The value or template passed as a parameter to the any2unichar function may be uninitialized, partially or completely initialized.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence names the function 'any2unichar', which does not exist; 'any2unistr' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:format-parameter
requirements.canonical: The optional `format` parameter of `any2unistr` IS used for the dynamic selection of how the resulting universal charstring is produced from `invalue`.
requirements.original: The optional format parameter is used for dynamic selection of how the resulting universal charstring should be produced from the provided invalue.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-any2unistr
requirements.condition: the format parameter is missing or is the empty string
requirements.canonical: When the `format` parameter of `any2unistr` is missing or is set to an empty string, the resulting universal charstring IS the same as the string produced by the `log` operation for the same operand.
requirements.original: When the optional format parameter is missing or is set to an empty string the resulting universal charstring is the same as the string produced by the log operation for the same operand.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-any2unistr
requirements.canonical: When the `format` parameter of `any2unistr` is "canonical", unbound fields SHALL be represented in the output as "-".
requirements.original: When the optional format parameter takes the value "canonical": unbound fields are represented in the output as "-", the fields and members of structured types are represented recursively in assignment notation.

ambiguity.issue: 'unbound' is not a TTCN-3 term; the glossary uses 'uninitialized'. The example shows that a completely uninitialized template is also represented as "-".

requirements.subject: ent:fn-any2unistr
requirements.canonical: When the `format` parameter of `any2unistr` is "canonical", the fields and members of structured types SHALL be represented recursively in assignment notation.
requirements.original: When the optional format parameter takes the value "canonical": unbound fields are represented in the output as "-", the fields and members of structured types are represented recursively in assignment notation.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-any2unistr
requirements.condition: format is neither "" nor "canonical" and the tool supports the custom format
requirements.canonical: When the `format` parameter of `any2unistr` is different from the empty string and "canonical" and the tool supports the specified custom format, the format of the result IS tool-specific.
requirements.original: If the actual value of the format parameter is different from the empty string and "canonical", the format of the result produced by the function is either tool-specific if the tool supports the specified custom format or it is the same as the string produced by the log operation (i.e. the same as if the parameter value was the empty string).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-any2unistr
requirements.condition: format is neither "" nor "canonical" and the tool does not support the custom format
requirements.canonical: When the `format` parameter of `any2unistr` is different from the empty string and "canonical" and the tool does not support the specified format, the result IS the same as the string produced by the `log` operation (as if the format parameter were the empty string).
requirements.original: If the actual value of the format parameter is different from the empty string and "canonical", the format of the result produced by the function is either tool-specific if the tool supports the specified custom format or it is the same as the string produced by the log operation (i.e. the same as if the parameter value was the empty string).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-any2unistr
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 apply to the `any2unistr` function.
requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.
